spec.description: NASA FIRMS's satellite fire detections (VIIRS, the last week) against the high-voltage grid from OpenStreetMap, in one of four regions: which lines a fire came near, how close and how often, played in pass by pass. Distances are measured in the region's equal-area projection. Data: NASA FIRMS, OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

spec.rawSql:
WITH r AS (
  SELECT * FROM (VALUES
      ('central-brazil', 'South_America', 'ESRI:102033', -25, -60, -2, -38, -13.5, -49),
      ('southern-africa', 'Southern_Africa', 'ESRI:102022', -22, 12, -5, 42, -13.5, 27),
      ('eastern-australia', 'Australia_NewZealand', 'EPSG:3577', -39, 138, -10, 154, -24.5, 146),
      ('california', 'USA_contiguous_and_Hawaii', 'EPSG:3310', 32.5, -124.5, 42, -114, 37.2, -119.3)
  ) v(region, firms, crs, s, w, n, e, lat, lng)
  WHERE region = ${region:sqlstring}
),
-- The region's lines of 200 kV and more, from OpenStreetMap, measured in the
-- region's equal-area projection.
grid AS (
  SELECT id, name, operator, kv, geom,
         ST_Transform(geom, 'EPSG:4326', r.crs, always_xy := true) AS xy
  FROM (
    SELECT e->>'id' AS id, coalesce(e->'tags'->>'name', e->'tags'->>'ref', 'OSM way ' || (e->>'id')) AS name,
           e->'tags'->>'operator' AS operator,
           try_cast(split_part(e->'tags'->>'voltage', ';', 1) AS INTEGER) // 1000 AS kv,
           ST_MakeLine(list_transform(json_extract(e, '$.geometry[*]')::JSON[],
                       p -> ST_Point((p->>'lon')::DOUBLE, (p->>'lat')::DOUBLE))) AS geom
    FROM (SELECT unnest(elements) AS e
          FROM read_json('http://feeds/overpass/power-lines/${region:raw}.json', columns = {elements: 'JSON[]'}))
  ), r
),
-- Every VIIRS detection in the region over the range, from the three satellites.
fires AS (
  SELECT latitude, longitude, frp, satellite, daynight,
         strptime(acq_date::VARCHAR || lpad(acq_time::VARCHAR, 4, '0'), '%Y-%m-%d%H%M')::TIMESTAMPTZ AS time,
         ST_Transform(ST_Point(longitude, latitude), 'EPSG:4326', r.crs, always_xy := true) AS xy
  FROM read_csv(['http://feeds/firms/noaa-20-viirs-c2/J1_VIIRS_C2_${firms:raw}_7d.csv',
                 'http://feeds/firms/noaa-21-viirs-c2/J2_VIIRS_C2_${firms:raw}_7d.csv',
                 'http://feeds/firms/suomi-npp-viirs-c2/SUOMI_VIIRS_C2_${firms:raw}_7d.csv'], union_by_name = true), r
  WHERE latitude BETWEEN r.s AND r.n AND longitude BETWEEN r.w AND r.e
    AND time BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
),
-- Each detection within the distance of a line, once per line.
near AS (
  SELECT f.time, f.latitude, f.longitude, f.satellite, f.frp, f.xy, g.id AS line_id, ST_Distance(f.xy, g.xy) / 1000 AS km
  FROM fires f JOIN grid g ON ST_DWithin(f.xy, g.xy, ${km:raw} * 1000)
),
exposed AS (
  SELECT g.id, g.name, g.operator, g.kv, count(*) AS detections, min(n.km) AS closest_km,
         max(n.frp) AS max_frp, max(n.time) AS last_seen,
         -- Fires snapped to 500 m first: thousands of points by a line are a few
         -- hundred cells, and their union is buffered in a fraction of the time.
         ST_Intersection(any_value(g.xy),
                         ST_Buffer(ST_Union_Agg(DISTINCT ST_Point(round(ST_X(n.xy) / 500) * 500, round(ST_Y(n.xy) / 500) * 500)),
                                   ${km:raw} * 1000, 4)) AS part,
         any_value(r.crs) AS crs
  FROM near n JOIN grid g ON g.id = n.line_id, r
  GROUP BY g.id, g.name, g.operator, g.kv
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM fires) AS "Fire detections",
       (SELECT count(DISTINCT (time, latitude, longitude, satellite)) FROM near) AS "Near a line",
       (SELECT count(DISTINCT line_id) FROM near) AS "Line sections exposed",
       (SELECT round(sum(ST_Length(part)) / 1000) FROM exposed) AS "Km of line exposed",
       (SELECT round(sum(ST_Length(xy)) / 1000) FROM grid) AS "Km of line mapped"

  FROM fires f JOIN grid g ON ST_DWithin(f.xy, g.xy, ${km:raw} * 1000)

marks AS (
  SELECT line_id, time, round(ST_X(xy) / 500) * 500 AS x, round(ST_Y(xy) / 500) * 500 AS y,

FROM marks m JOIN grid g ON g.id = m.line_id, r

spec.description: Every fire detection, coloured by its radiative power (MW), and the region's lines of 200 kV and more: dim, and red along the stretches a fire came within the chosen distance of. Press ▶ on the bar to play the satellite passes in: the fires and the red stretches build up together. Data: NASA FIRMS (VIIRS), OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
